findings.passage: “What I get upset about is when we have either legislators or people like my opponent come in and want to upend that process and make it more difficult for voters to access their right to vote when they have absolutely zero evidence that there are issues or fraud in the current process. We know it’s working well, and I think it’s an insult to our election workers, our election officials and the voters themselves.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Weirton Daily Times during an August 2026 campaign stop at the Jefferson County board of elections. She speaks about election-law changes that make voting harder, without naming photo ID in this passage. The same story says she was not in favor of State Issue 3 (the photo-ID constitutional amendment); that sentence is the reporter's paraphrase, not saved as her words.

findings.passage: “I think, right now, Ohio has a very good process. I do agree with the current secretary of state that we are the gold standard,” Russo, a resident of the Columbus suburb of Upper Arlington, said. “We have elections that are run by dedicated local election officials. We have Republicans and Democrats who are part of the process. Everything has a check and balance. We have a lot of security in the process.
findings.note: Quoted by the Weirton Daily Times in August 2026 on the security of Ohio's current election process.

findings.passage: “Maintaining accurate voter rolls matters, but not at the cost of eligible citizens losing their right to vote,” she said.
findings.note: Quoted by BG Independent News at a Bowling Green campaign event (page date taken from the page; event was the Saturday before). On voter-roll maintenance versus eligible voters.
